YEAR OLD MALE WITH CHEIF COMPLAINTS OF FEVER, ALTERED SENSORIUM FROM 1 MONTH"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(137, 137, 137); color: #898989; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #444444; font-family: \u0026quot;open sans\u0026quot;;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS\/HER GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(137, 137, 137); color: #898989;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial; font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA 57-year-old male resident of Nalgonda security guard by occupation came with the chief complaints of fever since 1-month, generalised weakness since 1 month and altered sensorium 1 month back for 3 days.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #757575; font-family: arial; font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117);\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #757575; font-family: arial; font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHe is apparently alright before 5 yrs then he developed neck pain which is insidious in onset gradually progressive dragging type associated with muscle spasms and clicking, popping sensation in the neck and backache which was also dull and aching pain with not able get up easily from bed and then after he developed dizziness, weakness, tingling and numbness in both the hands and legs and loss of bowel and bladder control. Bowel cleared through enema and bladder through urinary catheter. For this diagnosis is made as cervical and lumbar spondylosis and advised to undergo surgery. In this period he was diagnosed as hypertensive, but no\u0026nbsp;regular treatment was given to him. Surgery was done for cervical spondylosis and conservatively managing for lumbar spondylosis.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial; font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575;\"\u003EPatient developed generalised weakness 1 month with blurring of vision which was insidious on onset not progressive, after 2 days he developed fever which was 103 degrees. Fever was insidious in onset, gradually progressive no aggravating and relieving factors known. After two days of onset of fever he suddenly fell in bathroom due to weakness in legs and hurt his head. Upon approaching the patient family observed slurring of speech. He was then taken to government hospital. He approached the car by himself walking with the help of a stick during the travel to hospital he showed symptoms of altered sensorium where he was responding lately. He was kept in ward and treated only with glucose without any medications. He was then taken to a private hospital where his condition worsened and was unable to remember things which happened 10 mins back and could not recognise anyone except his elder daughter. As he was being taken to MRI, he lost consciousness and completely stopped responding. MRI was taken and high dose antibiotics were given where he regained consciousness and could slowly start recognizing his family members. There he was treated strong enough to transport to our hospital. They did an elective tracheostomy and sent him to our hospital. Upon reaching our hospital CSF analysis were done and treatment was started. Fever subsided completely and he was afebrile for a week. After a week into the treatment, he developed shortness of breath, he started developing pneumothorax to which a inter coastal drainage tube was placed. He was on ventilator for some time after this episode. Later 3 days after pneumothorax the patient developed a bed sore and along with-it developed fever. This time it was continuous gradually progressive relieved on medication.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117);\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;No history of loss of\u0026nbsp;coordination and unsteadiness while walking. No history of nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation abdominal pain. No h\/o decreased in urine, blood in urine, pus in the urine.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: arial; sans\u0026quot;;\"\u003ENOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS\/HER GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWelcome,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI am Dushyanth Reddy, an aspiring medical student would like to share some experience with Internal medicine and surgery in my career. Its possible with collaboration with department of internal medicine and other departments.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMy interest in medicine has came since childhood where my grandmother and grandfather has suffered congestive heart failure; and ventricular septal defect in my neighbourhood which is a acyanotic heart disease where in layman terms called as hole in the heart. My other grandfather suffered from emphysema which is a type of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and died from it. I would like to deal with cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases that are most commonly seen in my life.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere I would like to share some diseases about the third space fluid loss such heart failure, renal failure, pleural effusion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn these cases there is extravasation of fluid from vascular compartment into interstitial space which may due to increase in hydrostatic pressure or decrease in plasma oncotic pressure or lymphatic obstruction.This causes decrease in volume in vascular compartment. This causes edema, ascites, pleural effusion, facial edema. here are the links of cases this topic:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/06\/a-45-year-old-female-with-sob.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/06\/a-45-year-old-female-with-sob.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/08\/a-55-yr-old-man-presented-with.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/08\/a-55-yr-old-man-presented-with.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/11\/32-year-old-male-with-pleural-effusion.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/11\/32-year-old-male-with-pleural-effusion.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/09\/35-year-old-female-sobfever-generalized.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/dushyanthreddyrollno196.blogspot.com\/2022\/09\/35-year-old-female-sobfever-generalized.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnother interesting case is about liver abcess:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003ELiver abscess is an inflammatory space‐occupying lesion of the liver caused by infectious agents. Amoebic liver abscess (ALA) and pyogenic liver abscess (PLA) are its two predominant causes. Rarely, liver abscess can be caused by fungi, mycobacteria, and other atypical organisms. ALA is the predominant cause of liver abscess in India, seen in more than 60% of cases.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 0; position: relative; top: -0.5em; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003E\u003Ca aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-haspopup=\"true\" class=\"bibr popnode\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8518335\/#cld1128-bib-0001\" rid=\"cld1128-bib-0001\" role=\"button\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit; color: #4c2c92;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;1\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003EIt is caused by\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cem style=\"box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003EEntamoeba histolytica\u003C\/em\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;with feco‐oral route, the predominant mode of transmission.
